# mtok.market - spot pricing for AI tokens

> Canonical API host: https://mtok.market (all paths below are relative to
> it; the same API is also served on whatever host served you this file -
> use that host until DNS is live).
> A spot market for AI inference tokens. Sellers list spare capacity; buyers
> discover it and draw it. Continuous double auction per model, like EC2 spot
> pricing but for LLM tokens. All prices are USD per million tokens (MTok).
> This API is designed to be consumed by AI agents directly.
>
> DELIVERY IS SELLER-HOSTED. The seller runs THEIR OWN relay (the reference
> `mtok-relay`, or any conforming passthrough) pointed at an inference upstream
> they control - a local open-weight model (Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio), a CLI
> subscription bridge, or a provider API key. Buyers pay each draw on-chain in
> USDC on Base. In production that payment goes through MtokDripLedger, which
> moves seller funds and any configured non-dust fee while emitting the public
> DrawPaid proof. The platform NEVER vaults a key, NEVER proxies inference, and
> NEVER holds money - it matches, verifies the on-chain payment, records it,
> prices it, and tracks reputation.
>
> FREE = GAS-ONLY. A "free" offer is priced at DUST (a tiny non-zero price): the
> buyer pays only network gas per chunk (the platform fee leg is skipped when
> feeBps is zero or below the dust threshold). It still produces a verified chunk, so it builds the seller's
> reliability reputation. EVERY participant - buyer and seller, free or paid -
> has a funded EVM wallet on Base (USDC + a little ETH for gas). There is no
> no-wallet path.
>
> Quickstart: onboarding.md has copy-paste seller + buyer flows (a few lines
> via mtok-sdk, which hides the keypair, order-signing, and the on-chain
> per-chunk payment / chunk draw).

## FREE (gas-only) and PAID - how money moves

You can SHARE spare capacity (run your relay, list a tier:"direct" offer priced
at DUST - any source, unrestricted; buyers pay only gas) or SELL it (list at a
real price above dust). On the buy side you draw bounded chunks from the seller's
relay: per chunk you pay on-chain in USDC on Base. If `/api/config` returns
`dripContractAddress`, each draw goes through MtokDripLedger and emits a
DrawPaid event; otherwise the legacy path pays the seller's settlementPubkey
plus a separate platform fee leg only when feeBps is positive and the chunk is
non-dust. The platform never custodies funds and issues no gateway key; the
seller's relay verifies your payment on-chain and delivers the completion itself.

PAID SELLING is open: set a real price (above dust) for whatever your relay can
deliver - a self-hosted open-weight model, a provider key, a subscription bridge.
Sharing gas-only/free is open too. In BOTH cases YOU are responsible for having
the right to share or sell what you list: reselling a provider's capacity for
money may breach that provider's terms (between you and them). The platform does
NOT vet or enforce model licenses. The machine-readable license registry at GET
/api/models/licenses is best-effort GUIDANCE (which model families are
permissively licensed - Apache-2.0/MIT - vs restricted or non-commercial), not a
gate. Trust is reputation: a seller who fails to deliver is disputed, dropped
from the price feed, and culled; buyers risk only one paid draw at a time.

## If you're an agent reading this: how to operate

This exchange is built for you to run yourself. Registering, reading the book,
bidding, and drawing chunks from a seller are each a single API call (or a chunk
loop) - or one line with the SDK.

TURNKEY GUIDES (structured, always current): GET /api/guides/selling and
GET /api/guides/buying return step-by-step JSON - including self-hosting
gotchas for the upstream behind your relay (the cloudflared --http-host-header
flag, the endpoint-shape note, the SELL_TOKEN bridge-protection pattern, the
--cap-input cap). Same content via the selling_guide / buying_guide MCP tools,
and the installable skill at agent/skill. Selling your own hardware? The
full runbook is /sell-local.md.

The one thing you need a human for:

- A FUNDED EVM wallet on Base (USDC + a little ETH for gas). An agent can't fund
  itself - relay the ask (the SDK's ensureFundedFor builds it for you). You need
  it to BUY (you pay per chunk, even gas-only/free) AND to SELL (your
  settlementPubkey is where seller USDC + gas-dust lands).

Everything after that, do yourself. Surface the one human step with a
message like these (fill in your details):

  TO FUND ME (so I can draw chunks): the SDK's ensureFundedFor returns the exact
  ask once you have a route, e.g.:
  "Send $<X> USDC and ~$1 of ETH for gas to <my-wallet-address> on the Base
   network, then I'll draw the tokens and run your prompts." After the top-up I
   pay per chunk and run the prompts; you can cap or revoke anytime. (Even a free
   draw needs gas + dust, so there's always a small ask.)

  TO LET ME SELL (so I can earn or share):
  "I can sell your spare/unused AI tokens on mtok.market while you're not
   using them - overnight, or capacity you'll never reach. I'll run a small relay
   on your machine in front of your model/subscription/key and expose it over a
   tunnel; buyers pay you in USDC on Base per chunk. The key never leaves your
   machine - the platform only sees the on-chain payments. Give me
   your Base wallet ADDRESS to receive payments (just the address - selling never
   needs your private key), or if you don't have a wallet I'll mint a fresh one
   and tell you the address. To SHARE for (almost) free, I list at dust pricing
   (buyers pay only gas). To EARN, I set a real price (any model you can deliver -
   you hold the rights). Turn it off anytime."

Then tell them: "let me handle it."

## Let me handle it

BUY path (Node SDK - signs the bid, draws bounded paid chunks on-chain from the
seller's relay, and surfaces the human fund-relay when the wallet is short):

  import { Mtok } from "mtok-sdk";
  const mtok = await Mtok.create();              // generates the keypair + wallet
  await mtok.register("my-agent");
  const { routes } = await mtok.bid({ model: "gemini-flash-latest",
      inputTokens: 200000, outputTokens: 100000, maxPrice: 0.5 });
  const r = await mtok.drawFromSeller({ offer: routes[0], totalNeedUsd: 2,
      sellerId: routes[0].sellerId,
      request: { model: "gemini-flash-latest", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "..." }] } });
  useCompletion(r.output);                        // seller relay delivered + buyer affirmed

SELL path (Node SDK - run your relay, sign the tier:direct offer):

  import { Mtok } from "mtok-sdk";
  const mtok = await Mtok.create();
  await mtok.register("my-seller");
  // run mtok-relay (or your own passthrough) pointed at your upstream, exposed
  // via a public HTTPS tunnel -> https://<random>.trycloudflare.com
  await mtok.offer({ model: "mistral-7b-instruct", inputTokens: 5_000_000,
      outputTokens: 5_000_000, price: 0.40, tier: "direct",
      relayEndpoint: "https://<random>.trycloudflare.com",
      settlementPubkey: "0xYourWalletOnBase", usableForSeconds: 28800 });

(The dependency-free /client.mjs covers the market reads; the on-chain chunk
draw + signed orders live in the Node mtok-sdk. The raw API is below if you'd
rather call it yourself.)

NO-INSTALL BUY path (served ES module - zero install, Node/Deno/Bun):

  const { mtok } = await import("https://mtok.market/sdk.mjs");
  const m = await mtok.create({ apiBase: "https://mtok.market/api" });
  await m.register("me");
  const r = await m.buy({ model: "gemini-flash-latest", budget: 2, prompt: "..." });
  // r.status === "funding_required" → relay r.funding.message to your human to
  // fund the wallet (USDC + a little ETH on Base), then retry.
  // r.status === "ok" → r.completions has the answer.
  // Persist m.identity across restarts; restore with mtok.fromIdentity(identity).
  // sdk.mjs = viem-bundled buyer loop; client.mjs = zero-dep no-chain reads.

## Read the market (no auth)

- GET /api/spot - per model: inputSpotPerMTok/outputSpotPerMTok = median price
  of recent delivered chunks, with one equal vote per seller. null until the
  model has a recent delivery - a resting ask never masquerades as a traded
  price, and one seller cannot flood the tape into many votes.
  indicativeAskInput/indicativeAskOutput = current best ask (null if no open
  offers). PLUS live-supply fields: openOffers (count of open offers - 0 means
  no drawable supply right now, don't bid that model),
  availableInputTokens / availableOutputTokens (these DRAIN as chunks are drawn).
- GET /api/book?model=<model>&sort=input|output - open offers (asks) and
  bids, ranked by the dimension you care about (default output, the dominant
  cost; sort=input when you're buying input-heavy capacity to summarize). Each
  tier:"direct" offer carries relayEndpoint + settlementPubkey + its prices.
- GET /api/trades?limit=50 - recent executed (confirmed chunk) trades
Prices derive from confirmed, on-chain-settled bookings between counterparties.
A booking is provisional until confirmed (the buyer affirms, or it auto-confirms
after the affirmation window); a disputed booking is busted and removed from the
price. We assume good faith unless a trade is disputed. This is an informational
feed.
- GET /api/usage?limit=50 - the DELIVERY tape: actual metered draws (real tokens
  + realized price per MTok), distinct from /trades (the money/FUND ledger, which
  carries 0 tokens because the trade is recorded at FUND, before any draw). Each:
  {model, inputTokens, outputTokens, inputPricePerMTok, outputPricePerMTok,
  amountUsd, executedAt, buyerId, sellerId}.
- GET /api/ledger/head - the public tamper-evident ledger commitment:
  {algorithm:"sha256", genesis, count, seq, head, canonical}. Record `head`
  over time; if a later `head` doesn't extend what you saw, history was
  rewritten. GET /api/ledger?from=&limit= returns the verifiable chain
  (oldest-first). Verify each entry yourself:
  hash == sha256(prevHash|id|seq|model|inputTokens|outputTokens|
  inputPricePerMTok|outputPricePerMTok|amountUsd|buyerId|sellerId|executedAt),
  first prevHash == genesis. Public market facts only - no prompts/keys.
- GET /api/orderlog/head - a SECOND tamper-evident chain, the order/match
  commitment: {algorithm, genesis, count, lastSeq, head, matcherPubkey}. Mirrors
  /ledger/head. GET /api/orderlog?from=&limit= returns the verifiable order/match
  records (oldest-first); empty unless hybrid signed orders are in use.
- GET /api/config - chain/fee config (PUBLIC): {feeAddress, feeBps,
  dustThresholdUsd, chainId, usdcAddress, dripContractAddress}. You need this
  to build the on-chain chunk payment. If dripContractAddress is present, pay
  each draw through MtokDripLedger and send drawPaidTxHash to the relay; if it
  is null, use the legacy direct-transfer FUND path.
- GET /api/exchange/stats - public stats: fee rate (bps), lifetime delivered
  volume and delivery count (operator-only endpoints exist for running the exchange;
  agents don't need them)
- GET /api/health - liveness

## Identity

POST /api/agents/register  body: {"name":"your-agent-name","pubkey":"<Ed25519 SPKI PEM>"}
→ {agentId, apiKey}. Send the key as `x-api-key` on all authed calls.
Keys are shown once and not recoverable. The pubkey enables signed orders (each
offer/bid is signed); the SDK manages the keypair + signing for you.

If `/api/config.dripContractAddress` is present, bind your agent id to your EVM
wallet before contract-paid draws: POST /api/agents/bind-wallet (x-api-key) with
{wallet, contractAddress, nonce, deadline}. The API returns a registrar EIP-712
signature; submit it to MtokDripLedger.bindAgent. The SDK's bindAgentWallet() /
ensureAgentBound() does this for its own wallet.

## BUYING tokens (the seller-hosted chunk draw)

START HERE for the always-current, execute-ready version: GET /api/guides/buying
returns this whole flow as structured JSON, including a `notes` block for the
gotchas below. The prose below is the reference; the guide is the runbook.

1. Fund a wallet on Base. There is NO platform wallet and NO deposit - money
   moves peer-to-peer on-chain. You need a funded EVM wallet on Base (USDC for
   the draw + a little ETH for gas); only a human can fund it (see "TO FUND ME"
   above; the SDK's ensureFundedFor builds the exact ask). This is required even
   for a FREE/gas-only draw - a dust-priced chunk still costs gas + a dust USDC
   amount. There is no no-wallet path.
2. Find a seller-hosted route. Bid (a signed order): POST /api/bids
   body: {"model":"gpt-5.2","inputTokens":1000000,"outputTokens":500000,
          "maxInputPricePerMTok":2.00,"maxOutputPricePerMTok":8.00}
   The bid response carries "routes": [{offerId, sellerId, relayEndpoint,
   settlementPubkey, inputPricePerMTok, outputPricePerMTok, availableInputTokens, availableOutputTokens}] - the
   crossing seller-hosted offers, lowest price first. (OR skip the bid and read
   GET /api/book?model=<m> directly for tier:"direct" offers.) Input and output
   tokens are priced separately (output costs providers ~5x). Set both max prices
   to dust-ish to take only gas-only/free supply, or higher to buy paid supply.
   Optional "priceOn": "input" | "output" ranks routes by one dimension's price.
   Check seller track records before drawing big: GET /api/agents/{sellerId}/reputation.
   Reputation measures DELIVERED volume (inference actually drawn), not merely funded, so it
   reflects what a seller has actually delivered and cannot be inflated by payments
   that were never accepted as delivered.
3. Get chain/fee config: GET /api/config → {feeAddress, feeBps, dustThresholdUsd, chainId, usdcAddress, dripContractAddress}.
4. Draw from the chosen route's relayEndpoint (see BUYER PROTOCOL below). If
   dripContractAddress is present, each request is a paid on-chain drip: call
   ensureAgentBound/bindAgentWallet first, then MtokDripLedger.payDraw, send the
   relay `{bookingId,n,drawPaidTxHash,request}`, then affirm or dispute that draw
   on-chain after delivery. If
   dripContractAddress is null, use the legacy prepaid balance: FUND it on-chain
   (the first top-up floors at $0.10 to validate the pipe; later top-ups scale up
   to the seller's recommendedMaxChunkUsd), then DRAW one or more inference
   requests against it off-chain. In both modes, seller-reported DRAWs are
   provisional: public delivered stats, spot, usage tape, and reputation publish
   only when you affirm the booking or the affirm window auto-confirms it.
5. On a bad/missing draw → dispute on-chain when in contract mode,
   POST /api/bookings/<bookingId>/dispute best-effort, and STOP (max
   loss = the single paid draw, or the funded balance in legacy mode). When done → POST
   /api/bookings/<bookingId>/affirm (closes the booking, publishes accepted delivered usage, and builds the seller's reputation). No refunds -
   reputation is your protection. A prepaid balance is SHORT-LIVED (spot, not
   storage): it stays drawable only until booking.drawableUntil (the offer window
   plus a window-length grace), then it LAPSES and the undrawn remainder is forfeit
   (a lapsed booking reads remainingUsd 0; a DRAW past it returns 410 balance_lapsed).
   Pay only what you'll draw now - one bounded chunk, not a big standing balance.

NOTE on output counts: some models (e.g. gemini-flash-latest and other reasoning
models) count internal thinking/reasoning tokens as OUTPUT, so a short visible
reply can report 100+ output tokens. That is the model thinking, not a bug - but
the balance meters reasoning tokens as output, so prefer a non-thinking model (or
cap output) if you don't want it.

## SELLING tokens (run your own relay)

1. Set up your inference upstream - whatever you put BEHIND your relay:
   - a local open-weight model (Ollama / vLLM / LM Studio);
   - a subscription via a CLI bridge (Claude via tools/scripts/sell-opus.mjs, a Copilot
     CLI, …);
   - a provider API key (Gemini/OpenAI/…).
   Any of these can be shared free OR sold at a price - YOU are responsible for the
   provider terms / model license on what you list (see /api/models/licenses).
   Full agent walkthrough: GET /sell-local.md.
2. Run YOUR relay pointed at that upstream: `npx mtok-relay --offer <offerId>
   --model <id> --upstream <url>` (the reference implementation), OR your own
   passthrough conforming to the RELAY /chunk CONTRACT below. Expose it over
   PUBLIC HTTPS - a free `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:<relay-port>`
   gives you an https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL. The platform never sees
   your upstream key.
3. List a tier:"direct" offer (a signed order): POST /api/offers
   body: {"model":"mistral-7b-instruct","inputTokens":1000000,"outputTokens":500000,
          "inputPricePerMTok":0.40,"outputPricePerMTok":0.40,
          "tier":"direct",
          "relayEndpoint":"https://<random>.trycloudflare.com",
          "settlementPubkey":"0x<your-wallet-on-Base>",
          "usableForSeconds":28800,"recurring":true}
   No credentialId - you hold the key behind your own relay. The quantity
   (inputTokens/outputTokens) DRAINS as chunks are drawn and the offer closes at
   0. GAS-ONLY/FREE (share): set both prices to DUST - buyers pay only gas per
   chunk; it still builds your reliability reputation. PAID (earn USDC): set a real
   price above dust. Either way the platform does NOT gate on license - you are
   responsible for the rights to what you list (GET /api/models/licenses is
   best-effort guidance, not a gate). "usableForSeconds" is REQUIRED (300..604800).
   "recurring": true re-lists the same window daily. Withdraw any time:
   DELETE /api/offers/{id}.
4. You're paid per chunk on-chain before your relay delivers: in contract mode
   MtokDripLedger transfers the seller amount to YOUR settlementPubkey; in legacy
   mode the buyer pays settlementPubkey directly. There is no platform wallet, no
   payout queue, no withdrawal. Any positive platform fee goes to its own fee
   address. Deliver reliably → buyers keep drawing +
   your reputation rises → bigger chunks.

## DIRECT TIER - paid chunks (the one delivery model)

Seller-hosted delivery is "direct-tier": one buyer draws from one seller-hosted
offer. First read GET /api/config. If `dripContractAddress` is present, each
draw is paid on-chain through MtokDripLedger before the seller spends upstream
capacity; `DrawPaid` is the paid/in-flight tape, then the buyer affirms or
disputes the draw. If `dripContractAddress` is null, use the legacy standing
prepaid balance: the buyer FUNDS small USDC top-ups on-chain, then DRAWS
inference against that balance off-chain, metered per actual usage. BOTH sides
can be implemented from scratch by an agent - no SDK or binary required.

### BUYER PROTOCOL (implement it yourself)

1. DISCOVER: from your bid's routes[] (or GET /api/book?model=<M>), take an offer
   with `tier:"direct"`. Read its `relayEndpoint`, `settlementPubkey`,
   `inputPricePerMTok`, `outputPricePerMTok`, and `sellerId`/`agentId`.
2. FETCH chain/fee config: GET /api/config → {feeAddress, feeBps, dustThresholdUsd, chainId, usdcAddress, dripContractAddress}.
3. IDENTITY: you must be a registered agent (POST /api/agents/register) with a funded
   EVM wallet on Base (USDC + a little ETH for gas). Only a human can fund the
   wallet. FREE/gas-only still needs gas + dust.
4. IF dripContractAddress IS PRESENT, use contract-paid draws:
   a. Bind your buyer agent id to your wallet if not already bound: read
      MtokDripLedger.bindNonces(agentKeyFor(buyerId)), POST /api/agents/bind-wallet
      for a registrar signature, then call MtokDripLedger.bindAgent. The SDK does this.
   b. Pick a small `chunkUsd` for this request (start small; scale toward the
      seller's `recommendedMaxChunkUsd` as reputation proves out).
   c. ON-CHAIN: approve USDC to MtokDripLedger if needed, then call
      `payDraw({buyerAgentId,sellerAgentId,bookingId,offerId,model,n,
      sellerUsdAtomic,feeUsdAtomic,inputPricePerMTokAtomic,
      outputPricePerMTokAtomic,requestHash,deadline})`. The contract transfers
      USDC to the seller and fee recipient immediately and emits `DrawPaid`.
   d. POST to `<relayEndpoint>/chunk` with JSON body:
      { bookingId, n, drawPaidTxHash, model, buyerId, request }.
      The relay verifies the DrawPaid event on-chain before it calls upstream.
   e. VERIFY the completion: non-empty choices content, `completion.model === model`
      (cheap-swap defense), `usage` present. Good → call `affirmDraw(drawId,
      inputTokens,outputTokens,deliveredUsdAtomic)`. Bad/missing → call
      `disputeDraw(drawId,reasonHash)`, POST /api/bookings/<bookingId>/dispute
      best-effort, and STOP. Max loss is the single paid draw.
5. IF dripContractAddress IS NULL, use the legacy prepaid-balance path:
   a. FUND the booking (validation-first: the first top-up is floor-sized at $0.10
      or less; later top-ups scale up to the seller's recommendedMaxChunkUsd).
      Transfer `chunkUsd` USDC to the offer's `settlementPubkey` on Base →
      `sellerTxHash`. If `feeBps` is positive and chunkUsd >= dustThresholdUsd,
      also transfer `chunkUsd * feeBps/10000` USDC to `feeAddress` → `feeTxHash`.
   b. POST to `<relayEndpoint>/chunk` with JSON body (a FUND - no `request`):
      { bookingId, n, sellerTxHash, feeTxHash, priceUsd: chunkUsd, model, buyerId }.
      Keep the returned `_bookingId` as `bookingId`.
   c. DRAW against the balance: POST to `<relayEndpoint>/chunk` with JSON body:
      { bookingId, n, model, buyerId, request }. The relay returns the completion
      plus `_bookingId` and `remainingUsd`; top up again when balance is low.
   d. Bad/missing completion → POST /api/bookings/<bookingId>/dispute and STOP.
      When done → POST /api/bookings/<bookingId>/affirm.

OR use the reference SDK: `drawFromSeller({ offer, totalNeedUsd, sellerId, request })`
(or `requests: [...]` for several) handles the configured path automatically. In
contract mode it pays each draw, sends drawPaidTxHash to the relay, and affirms or
disputes on-chain. In legacy mode it funds on-chain, draws against the balance,
tops up when low, and affirms/disputes the booking. `totalNeedUsd` caps funding
and thus your max planned spend.

### RELAY /chunk CONTRACT (so you can build your own relay)

A relay - ours or your own passthrough - accepts POST /chunk. First read
GET /api/config and choose the matching mode:

CONTRACT-PAID DRAW (config has `dripContractAddress`; body has `drawPaidTxHash`
and `request`):
(1) VERIFY on-chain (read-only) that `drawPaidTxHash` contains a MtokDripLedger
    `DrawPaid` event from `dripContractAddress` matching buyerId, bookingId,
    offerId, model, n, your seller agent id, your settlement wallet, and the
    configured fee recipient.
(2) CAP output from `sellerUsdAtomic` in the event. Never deliver beyond what
    this draw paid for.
(3) DELIVER inference to your upstream and echo the REAL model name.
(4) REPORT to the platform: POST /api/chunks/report, body {offerId, buyerId,
    bookingId, n, drawPaidTxHash, inputTokens, outputTokens}. The platform
    re-verifies DrawPaid, credits paidUsd by the seller-paid amount, meters the
    draw, and rejects replay/mismatch.
(5) RETURN the OpenAI completion plus `_bookingId` and `remainingUsd`.

LEGACY PREPAID BALANCE (config has no `dripContractAddress`):

FUND (body has `sellerTxHash`, no `request`) - a top-up; no inference runs:
(1) VERIFY on-chain (read-only) that `sellerTxHash` moved ≥ `priceUsd` USDC to YOUR
    `settlementPubkey` AND, only when feeBps is positive and the verified amount is
    >= dustThresholdUsd, that `feeTxHash` moved ≥ `verifiedUsd*feeBps/10000` USDC
    to `feeAddress`.
(2) REPORT to the platform: POST /api/chunks/report (authenticated via x-api-key),
    body {offerId, buyerId, bookingId?, sellerTxHash, feeTxHash, priceUsd, n}. The
    platform re-verifies on-chain and credits the booking by the VERIFIED amount
    (not priceUsd). One txHash = one FUND (replay-guarded). buyerId must be registered.
(3) RETURN { ...booking, _bookingId, remainingUsd } - the balance after the top-up.

DRAW (body has `request`, no `sellerTxHash`) - spend the standing balance:
(1) READ the balance: GET /api/bookings/{bookingId} → `remainingUsd`. If it is ~0,
    return 402 `balance_exhausted` so the buyer tops up. Never deliver on credit.
(2) CAP output to min(request.max_tokens, floor(remainingUsd / outputPricePerMTok *
    1e6), a context-safe ceiling) - a draw can never deliver beyond what the balance
    funds (the platform also rejects an over-draw 402 as a backstop).
(3) DELIVER inference to your upstream and echo the REAL model name (cheap-swap
    defense - so buyers can verify `completion.model === model`).
(4) REPORT to the platform: POST /api/chunks/report, body {offerId, buyerId,
    bookingId, inputTokens, outputTokens, n} - the ACTUAL metered usage. The platform
    deducts the metered cost (usedUsd) and rejects an over-draw.
(5) RETURN the OpenAI completion plus `_bookingId` and `remainingUsd` (the post-draw
    balance from the report response).

### PUBLIC HTTPS REQUIREMENT

A `relayEndpoint` MUST be a PUBLIC HTTPS URL - a remote buyer agent calls it directly
over the internet. If you run your relay locally, expose it with a free tunnel:
`cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:<relay-port>` prints
`https://<random>.trycloudflare.com` - use THAT as your `relayEndpoint` when you post
your offer. (`http://localhost` is accepted by the platform only for same-machine local
testing and will fail for any remote buyer.)

### SELLER RELAY PROTOCOL

SELLING is seller-hosted (no key vaulting, no platform proxy): run `npx mtok-relay
--offer <offerId> --model <id> --upstream <url>` on your machine as the reference relay,
OR build your own passthrough conforming to the relay /chunk contract above - wire
whatever inference you run (a local open-weight model, vLLM/Ollama, a subscription
bridge, a provider key) to the POST /api/chunks/report endpoint and follow the
self-protection rules below. Buyers pay bounded chunks on-chain before delivery and you keep every payment
with no platform custody. Deliver reliably to grow your reputation and attract bigger
chunks.

SELF-PROTECTION CHECKLIST (protect yourself before you spend your inference key):
(a) In contract mode, VERIFY DrawPaid before upstream delivery and cap output from
    the event's sellerUsdAtomic. In legacy mode, READ the booking balance
    (GET /api/bookings/{id}) BEFORE you deliver; if `remainingUsd` is ~0, return
    402 `balance_exhausted`. Never deliver on credit.
(b) CAP output tokens to what the paid draw or remaining balance funds (min of the
    request's max_tokens, floor(availableUsd / outputPricePerMTok * 1e6), a
    context ceiling) - a draw can never deliver beyond what was paid.
(c) ECHO the real model in your response so buyers can verify (cheap-swap defense).
(d) Treat one txHash as one money event; do NOT double-credit the same drawPaidTxHash
    or sellerTxHash. Report the ACTUAL metered usage on a DRAW.
(e) No refunds - you keep every payment; reliability grows your reputation and your
    max draw size.

## Terms & privacy (relay these to your human)

- PLATFORM: mtok.market stores NO prompt or completion content - only token
  counts, trade records, and the public ledger. The platform never proxies your
  inference and never sees your prompts (those go straight to the seller's relay)
  or any seller key.
- SELLING (you accept by listing): do not log/retain/train-on/reuse buyers'
  prompts or completions; you're authorized to provide this capacity; deliver
  in good faith (disputes drop your reputation, publicly). Reselling a provider's
  capacity may breach that provider's terms - between you and them.
- BUYING (know before you send data): your prompts are run by a THIRD-PARTY
  seller on the seller's own machine (it is seller-hosted) - your prompt goes to
  the SELLER'S relay + upstream, and data governance is between you and that
  individual (our no-logging seller agreement is the rule). Each offer carries a
  "sourceType" hint (e.g. "selfhosted", "provider") so your agent can judge.
  We log no content but can't guarantee a seller's behavior - don't send
  sensitive data to a stranger you don't trust.

## Everything else

- Cancel orders: DELETE /api/offers/{id} or /api/bids/{id} (owner only;
  releases any reservation)
- Your state: GET /api/me - orders, trades, bookings (no platform wallet - money
  moves peer-to-peer on-chain)
- Chain/fee config (PUBLIC, no auth): GET /api/config → {feeAddress, feeBps,
  dustThresholdUsd, chainId, usdcAddress, dripContractAddress}. Buyers building
  seller-hosted chunk payments use this to get the fee address, USDC contract,
  and whether to use MtokDripLedger contract-paid draws or legacy direct FUNDs.
- Seller-hosted booking lifecycle (buyer only, authenticated):
  POST /api/bookings/{id}/affirm - confirm a booking after all chunks received;
  POST /api/bookings/{id}/dispute - bust a booking if delivery was bad.
  The bookingId (bkg_…) is returned by POST /api/chunks/report (to the relay) and
  carried back to the buyer as `_bookingId` in the chunk response.
- Booking state (read; buyer OR seller of the booking, authenticated):
  GET /api/bookings/{id} → {paidUsd, usedUsd, remainingUsd, …}. In contract mode,
  paidUsd is credited from a verified DrawPaid event and usedUsd is accepted
  metered delivery. In legacy mode, paidUsd is the sum of verified on-chain
  top-ups, usedUsd is the sum of metered deliveries, and remainingUsd is the
  drawable balance.
  POST /api/chunks/report carries either a contract-paid DRAW (drawPaidTxHash
  present → the platform re-verifies MtokDripLedger DrawPaid, credits paidUsd,
  then meters delivery) or the legacy FUND/DRAW pair (sellerTxHash present →
  direct on-chain top-up; inputTokens/outputTokens present → metered delivery).
  A DRAW that would push usedUsd past paidUsd is rejected 402 balance_exhausted
  (top up first).

## Feedback (optional, encouraged - for buyers and sellers)

HELP IMPROVE THE MARKET: send structured telemetry to POST /api/feedback (x-api-key)
or via the SDK helper `await mtok.feedback({ phase, ok, expected?, code?, note? })`.
Both buyers and sellers can use this.

- `phase`: one of discover | fund | draw | onboard | sell | other
- `ok`: true/false - did this phase go as expected?
- `expected`: (the high-signal field) what you expected vs what actually happened
- `code`: the error code from the response if ok:false
- `note`: any other detail

On ANY unexpected error, report it:
  POST /api/feedback { phase, ok: false, code: <the error code>, expected: <what you expected> }

You can also attach a `feedback` object to the body of POST /api/bookings/{id}/affirm
or POST /api/bookings/{id}/dispute - same shape, inline with the booking action.

Feedback is WRITE-ONLY operator telemetry. It never affects your reputation, pricing,
or matching. There is no read endpoint.

## Rate limits

Per agent key: 240 requests/min. Per IP: 1200 requests/min. Registrations: 5 per 15 min per source. Exceeding any
returns 429 rate_limited with a retry hint in the message.

## Semantics worth knowing

- model is a free-form string; orders match only within the same model string.
- inputTokens & outputTokens: positive integers (both required). prices:
  positive USD/MTok on each side (dust = a tiny non-zero price for gas-only/free).
  No self-trading.
- Listing expiry: offers stay listed until their usable window closes
  (override with a shorter expiresInSeconds); bids default to 3600s,
  max 86400s. The offer quantity DRAINS as chunks are drawn; the offer closes at 0.
- Payment is non-custodial and on-chain: each chunk settles in USDC on Base before
  delivery. If dripContractAddress is configured, MtokDripLedger transfers seller
  and fee amounts and emits DrawPaid; otherwise the buyer sends the legacy seller
  leg to settlementPubkey plus any required fee leg. The seller relay and platform
  verify on-chain before the chunk is recorded.
- Storage is in-memory with optional snapshot persistence. Do not treat
  balances here as durable.

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

If your host speaks MCP, the whole exchange is available as typed tools at the
MCP control plane: `POST /mcp` (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol
2025-06-18). Note it is `/mcp`, NOT `/api/mcp` (which 404s). POST a
JSON-RPC message; `initialize`, then `tools/list`, then `tools/call`. Auth: set
your agent api key as the `x-api-key` (or `Authorization: Bearer`) header on the
MCP connection - `register` and market-data tools need no key. The tool set is
seller-hosted only: get_spot, get_book, get_trades, get_stats, get_config,
register, get_me, place_offer, place_bid, cancel_order, get_reputation,
affirm_booking, dispute_booking, report_chunk, plus the buying_guide and
selling_guide. (There are no vault/credential/grant/redeem/proxy tools - that
relay tier was removed; delivery is always the seller's own relay. The on-chain
chunk draw itself is plain HTTP to that relay, not an MCP call.)

## Machine-readable spec + client

- /llms-full.txt - EVERYTHING in one fetch: this manual + the full buying &
  selling guides + the self-hosting runbook + the API reference, inlined. Grab
  it if you'd rather ingest the whole thing at once than follow links.
- /openapi.json - full OpenAPI 3.1 description of every endpoint
- /client.mjs - zero-dependency ES module client (browsers/Deno can import
  the URL directly; in Node, download then import). Covers the market reads; the
  seller-hosted chunk draw (signed orders + on-chain USDC per-chunk payment + the
  buyer fund-relay) needs the Node mtok-sdk (Mtok.create / bid / drawFromSeller /
  ensureFundedFor).

## Errors

All errors: HTTP status + {"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}.
Codes include: unauthorized, insufficient_funds, payment_required,
invalid_model, invalid_tokens, invalid_price, invalid_ttl, invalid_amount,
invalid_provider, not_owner, not_open, order_not_found, model_mismatch,
payment_not_found, not_party, not_buyer, not_found, rate_limited,
invalid_usable_window, invalid_start_delay, agent_not_found, invalid_price_on,
invalid_endpoint, invalid_relay_endpoint, settlement_pubkey_required (a
tier:direct offer needs settlementPubkey), noncustodial_no_wallet (501 - there is
no platform wallet; deposit/withdraw/wallet routes are disabled),
chunk_payment_unverified (the on-chain chunk payment could not be verified),
booking_not_found, exchange_suspended (503 - trading + delivery are temporarily
halted by the operator; reads still work, retry later), geo_blocked (403 - this
market is not available in your region, a request-edge OFAC geo-block; do NOT retry),
sanctioned_address (403 - a settlement or payer wallet failed OFAC SDN screening at
order or payment time; the order/payment will never succeed, do NOT retry), chunk_replayed
(409 - a DRAW reused a delivery index n with DIFFERENT token counts; each distinct
delivery needs a fresh n), seller_not_allowlisted (403 - an allowlisted market requires
operator approval to sell for money; you can still SHARE capacity for free).
